Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience.Synaptic physiology and plasticity: Experimental studies of synaptic transmission, short- and long-term plasticity, synaptic proteins, and mechanisms underlying learning at the cellular/synapse level (electrophysiology, optogenetics, super-resolution imaging).
Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience.Ion channels and membrane biology: Patch-clamp and imaging experiments characterizing channel functions, gating, trafficking, and roles in excitability and disease.
Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience.Neurotransmitter synthesis and metabolis: Biochemical and imaging experiments measuring neurotransmitter production, release, reuptake, and enzymatic pathways.
Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience.Cell type characterization and single ce: Single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and follow-up validation using in situ hybridization and targeted physiology.

Developmental Neuroscience.Neurogenesis and migration: In vivo and in vitro experiments on neuronal progenitors, lineage tracing, and mechanisms of neuronal migration and differentiation.
Developmental Neuroscience.Circuit formation and synaptogenesis: Experimental mapping of how connections form during development using imaging, electrophysiology, and genetic perturbations.
Developmental Neuroscience.Stem cells and reprogramming models: Experimental derivation and use of iPSC/embryonic stem cell models, organoids and transplantation assays to study development and disease.

Systems and Circuit Neuroscience.Sensory systems: Behavioral, electrophysiological, imaging, and perturbation experiments probing visual, auditory, somatosensory, olfactory and taste circuits.
Systems and Circuit Neuroscience.Motor control and action: In vivo recordings, stimulation, kinematic tracking, and closed-loop perturbation to study motor planning, control, and learning.
Systems and Circuit Neuroscience.Homeostatic and autonomic circuits: Experiments on circuits regulating sleep, appetite, thermoregulation, and autonomic outputs using physiology and neuromodulation.
Systems and Circuit Neuroscience.Rhythms representations and oscillations: Field-potential and unit recordings, optogenetic manipulation and modeling-informed validation of network rhythms and their functions.

Cognitive and Behavioral Neuroscience.Decision making and reward: Behavioral paradigms with concurrent neural recording/manipulation (animals and human) probing valuation, reinforcement learning, and choice.
Cognitive and Behavioral Neuroscience.Memory and learning: Experimental assays of encoding, consolidation, retrieval across scales (molecular to systems), often combining behavior, imaging and perturbation.
Cognitive and Behavioral Neuroscience.Attention and perception: Psychophysics, human neuroimaging, and animal electrophysiology experiments investigating attentional selection and perceptual processes.
Cognitive and Behavioral Neuroscience.Social and affective neuroscience: Empirical studies of social cognition, emotion, empathy and related neural circuits in humans and animal models.

Neurophysiology and Electrophysiology.In vivo extracellular recordings: Multi-unit, single-unit, and array recordings in awake/behaving animals (Neuropixels, silicon probes) and acute preparations.
Neurophysiology and Electrophysiology.Intracellular and patch clamp techniques: In vitro and in vivo patch recordings for synaptic/cellular physiology and intrinsic property measurements.
Neurophysiology and Electrophysiology.EEG ECoG and MEG experiments: Noninvasive/partially invasive electrical and magnetic recording in humans and animal models, used with stimulation and behavioral tasks.

Neuroimaging and Brain Mapping.MRI and fMRI: Human and animal structural and functional MRI studies, including task-based and resting-state fMRI and neurite microstructure imaging.
Neuroimaging and Brain Mapping.PET and molecular imaging: In vivo imaging of receptor binding, metabolism, and molecular pathology using PET tracers and related modalities.
Neuroimaging and Brain Mapping.Two photon and in vivo optical imaging: High-resolution calcium/voltage imaging and chronic window experiments in small animals to track activity across populations over time.

Connectomics and circuit mapping.Light level circuit tracing: Viral tracing, transsynaptic labels, and genetic reporters combined with mesoscale imaging to map connectivity.
Connectomics and circuit mapping.Electron microscopy connectomics: Serial-EM and reconstruction pipelines mapping synaptic-level connectivity; experimental validation of wiring diagrams.
Connectomics and circuit mapping.Diffusion MRI and tractography validatio: Comparative experiments linking tractography to ground-truth anatomy using ex vivo and animal correlates.

Neurogenetics and Genomics.Genetic models and CRISPR experiments: Creation and phenotyping of genetic animal models and CRISPR-based perturbations to test gene function in circuits and behavior.
Neurogenetics and Genomics.GWAS functional follow up: Experimental validation (e.g., gene perturbation, cellular phenotyping) of human genetic associations in model systems.
Neurogenetics and Genomics.Epigenetics and activity dependent regul: Experiments linking neural activity to chromatin/transcriptional changes using in vivo and in vitro assays.

Neuroimmunology and neuroinflammation.Microglia and glia functional experiment: In vivo imaging and manipulation of microglia, astrocytes and other glia to study roles in development, plasticity and disease.
Neuroimmunology and neuroinflammation.Peripheral immune brain interactions: Experimental studies of how systemic inflammation and immune signaling affect neural function and behavior.

Neurodegeneration and aging.Mechanisms of neurodegenerative diseases: Animal and cellular models, biomarker studies, and in vivo imaging experiments probing pathology and progression (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS, etc.).
Neurodegeneration and aging.Aging and brain function: Longitudinal and cross-sectional experimental studies of aging brain physiology, cognition, and resilience mechanisms.

Clinical and Translational Neuroscience.Neurology and neurotherapeutics research: Clinical trials, translational animal studies, biomarker development, and physiological monitoring related to neurological disorders.
Clinical and Translational Neuroscience.Neuropsychiatric translational research: Experimental interventions (pharmacologic, neuromodulation), biomarker validation, and clinical neurophysiology for psychiatric conditions.
Clinical and Translational Neuroscience.Neurorehabilitation and behavioral inter: Empirical trials of rehabilitation protocols, brain stimulation-assisted recovery, and outcome measurement studies.

Neuropharmacology and neurochemistry.Drug action and target validation: Preclinical experiments testing candidate compounds, receptor pharmacodynamics, and synaptic/network effects.
Neuropharmacology and neurochemistry.High throughput phenotypic screens: Cellular and organismal experimental screens for neuroactive compounds with follow-up mechanism-of-action studies.

Neurotechnology and Neural Engineering.Brain computer interfaces and implants: Experimental development and human/animal testing of invasive and noninvasive BCIs, signal decoding and closed-loop systems.
Neurotechnology and Neural Engineering.Neuromodulation and brain stimulation: TMS, DBS, focused ultrasound, transcranial electrical stimulation experiments in humans and animals, including closed-loop designs.
Neurotechnology and Neural Engineering.Neural recording and sensor development: Experimental engineering and validation of electrodes, optical probes, and wireless/miniature devices.

Comparative and Evolutionary Neuroscienc.Nonmodel and wild species experiments: Field and lab experimental studies of neural systems in diverse species to probe conserved principles and ethologically relevant behaviors.
Comparative and Evolutionary Neuroscienc.Evolution of neural circuits: Comparative experiments linking anatomy, physiology and behavior across species to infer evolutionary adaptations.

Sleep circadian and homeostatic neurosci.Sleep recording and manipulation: In vivo polysomnography, optogenetic/chemogenetic sleep manipulation, and studies of sleep-dependent memory processes.
Sleep circadian and homeostatic neurosci.Circadian rhythms experiments: Molecular and physiological experiments on cellular clocks, entrainment, and systemic effects across organisms.

Behavioral neuroscience and ethology.Naturalistic behavioral paradigms: Experimental designs measuring complex, natural behaviors with ethological relevance, often combined with neural recordings and manipulation.
Behavioral neuroscience and ethology.Learning paradigms and task development: Empirical development and use of standardized behavioral assays to probe learning, motivation, and cognition.

Methods tools and reproducibility.Optogenetics and chemogenetics validatio: Experimental application and rigorous benchmarking of optical and chemical tools for causal circuit interrogation.
Methods tools and reproducibility.Recording and analysis pipeline experime: Methodological experiments validating preprocessing, spike-sorting, imaging analysis, and open-data pipelines across labs.
Methods tools and reproducibility.Standards reproducibility and open resou: Empirical replication studies, multi-site validations, and creation/testing of shared datasets and protocols.
